subject: Private hosting action summary — Calyx Health (network/residency asks)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & notes from today — Private hosting constraints

Hi Sofia — thanks again for taking the time today. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key constraints and confirm next steps so we all have the same picture. If I missed anything, please flag it and we'll adjust.

Recap of pain points & must-haves
- Customer requirement: all production inference for PHI must remain inside the EU and be hosted in a private environment (VPC or on-prem).
- Network policy: no direct outbound internet from the inference hosts. Any egress must be through an approved bastion/proxy and limited to a whitelist of destinations (e.g., KMS endpoints, licensing/patch endpoints).
- Air-gap driver: regulatory audit will require demonstrable separation for the models handling PHI; intermittent data ingest (batch) is acceptable but real-time inference traffic must never traverse public internet.
- Security & compliance: SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001 evidence required; customer has a vendor questionnaire for us to complete (they'll share).
- Key management: customer prefers to bring their own keys (KMS/HSM) with rotation policies; Redwood must support customer-managed KMS in EU region.
- Audit/retention: retention of request logs and audit trails for 7 years (or exportable to their archival solution).

Technical constraints called out during the call
- No persistent outbound connections from inference hosts — we discussed a jump-hosting pattern where a small, tightly controlled egress proxy (managed by customer) handles signed requests to Redwood control plane.
- If on-prem: ability to run the Redwood Private package inside an isolated cluster with restricted egress and a pluggable KMS adapter.
- Network topology ask: they will provide a firewall rule matrix and subnet map; we need to validate port ranges and IP allowlist for the control plane.

Immediate next steps (action owners & tentative timeline)
1) Calyx to share: network diagram (subnets, firewalls), vendor security questionnaire, and procurement contact (Marco) — by Thu 19 Feb. [owner: Calyx]
2) Redwood to provide: SOW template + high-level hosting options (on-prem, VPC with egress broker, Hybrid) and a short tech appendix showing KMS/HSM options — by Fri 20 Feb. [owner: Redwood: Ava/Ben]
3) Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) to validate port/IP needs and KMS flows — propose Tue 24 Feb 09:00 or Wed 25 Feb 14:00 CET.
4) Procurement: Redwood to provide order-of-magnitude estimate for a 3-month POC and enterprise terms that reflect the private deployment model.

Attachments included: calyx_network_requirements.pdf (notes we took), redwood_sow_template_v2.docx (draft SOW).

Thanks — I'll prepare the draft SOW and options doc and loop Ben for the SE deep-dive.

Best,
Ava Chen

Hi Ava — thanks for the thorough recap, that matches our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

1) Egress: we do allow a managed egress proxy but it must terminate inside our DMZ. The proxy can call out to Redwood's control endpoints only on port 443 and must be locked to a set of IPs.
2) KMS: we use an on-prem HSM (Thales). We'll need an adapter and proof that key material never leaves our HSM.
3) Timeline: procurement approval for the POC will likely take 4–6 weeks after security signs off. We're aiming for a May POC kickoff, which aligns with your Q2 window.

I've attached the initial security questionnaire (calyx_security_questionnaire.xlsx) and our procurement contact is Marco (he's CC'd). I'll work on the network diagram and share by Thu.

On the deep-dive: Tue 24 Feb 09:00 CET works for our infra lead.

Sofia
